attorneys.name: Gerard M. Wrynn
attorneys.practice_type: Trusts and Estates Litigation; Planning and Administration Lawyers in Greenwich, CT
attorneys.bio:
Since 1988, Gerard M. Wrynnhas focused his practice in areas of wills, trusts and estates. With experience in all aspects of estate planning, trust and estate administration, including New York State Surrogate's Court Proceedings and proceedings in the Connecticut Probate Courts. Mr. Wrynn's expertise ranges from the simple to complex. His extensive experience dealign with the Internal Revenue Service, New York State Department of Taxation and Finance and the Connecticut Department of Revenue Services, on many varied matters, including the processing and audit of estate and gift tax returns, benefits clients at both the agent and appeals levels.

Active in legal circles, Mr. Wrynn is a member of the Probate and Trust Law Section of the American Bar Association, The Real Property, The Trust and Estates and Elder Law Sections of the New York State Bar Association, the Greenwich, Connecticut, Westchester County (NY), and Queens County (NY) Bar Associations. Sharing his broad knowledge with the community, he has lectured before numerous groups, corporations and associations regarding estate planning; including the American Institue of Certified Public Accountants; St. John's University Alumni and New York State Bar Association Membership. Mr. Wrynn also donates a generous amount of his time to charitable causes. In recognition of his pro bono work in the Town of Greenwich, CT, Mr. Wrynn was the 2011 recipient of the Pro Bono Award presented by the Hon. David L. Hopper, Probate Judge for the Town of Greenwich. He is also a member of the Board of Directors of the Beachside Soccer Club of CT Inc. in Norwalk, Connecticut.

attorneys.name: William B. Wynne
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in East Hartford, CT
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Wynne is a trial attorney with over 25 years of courtroom and appellate experience. He has tried cases to juries in the state and federal courts and has briefed and argued appellate cases in the fields of personal injury cases, health care law, civil rights and business law.

Bill received his B.A. Degree with Distinction in Political Science from the University of Connecticut in 1980. Prior to attending law school, he gained experience in the corporate world, working in the business department of the Bridgeport Post Publishing Company. He thereafter obtained his Juris Doctorate Degree at Drake University Law School, Des Moines, Iowa with Dean’s List Honors.

From the first week Bill was a lawyer, he has been in the courtroom, litigating cases. He has represented individuals, businesses, and insurance corporations. He has also litigated against corporations and governmental bureaucracies. He has published reported decisions in the state and federal courts.

Bill has also lectured at the Law and Psychiatry Annual Conference, taught paralegal courses and conducted legal seminars.

attorneys.name: Anthony Yorio
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Danbury, CT
attorneys.bio:
Contact me for information on: Real Estate, Personal Injury, Criminal Defense and Litigation.

Attorney Yorio primarily concentrates his practice in Real Estate, Personal Injury and Criminal Defense matters. Before entering private practice and founding Yorio Law Group, P.C., Attorney Yorio served as an Assistant District Attorney in the City of Philadelphia. Following public service, Attorney Yorio went into private practice where he focused primarily on litigation matters that spanned from Medical Malpractice to Business and Contract disputes. When he opened the firm in 2007, he decided to apply his trial experience to transactional matters, which inextricably led him to Real Estate where the market condition at the time was forcing countless homeowners into foreclosure. Attorney Yorio remains steadfastly dedicated to protecting his clients whether it be in a contract or the courtroom.

Attorney Yorio received a B.A. in Biology from Western Connecticut State University in 1997, a Masters degree in Public Health from Indiana University in 1998 and lis law degree from Indiana University—Bloomington in 2002. In addition to his extensive legal experience, Mr. Yorio is accomplished in the medical field. Having received his certificate as a paramedic in 1992, he has more than a decade of experience in emergency medical services as a paramedic, educator, and manager before entering law practice.

attorneys.name: Steven M. Zelman
attorneys.firm_name: Murphy, Laudati, Kiel and Alfano, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Wills Lawyers in Granby, CT
attorneys.bio:
Steven M. Zelman, Connecticut Judge of Probate (Ret.) focuses on probate administration, estate planning, real estate and commercial litigation. Judge Zelman retired as a Judge of Probate in August, 2017 after serving more than 26 years. Judge Zelman served as Judge of Probate for the Town of Bloomfield for 20 years and the Tobacco Valley Probate District for over six years after the Probate Courts in Connecticut were consolidated. In addition, Judge Zelman was appointed as Administrative Judge for the Hartford Regional Children’s Probate Court by the Connecticut Probate Administrator covering 28 towns in the Hartford area. He served in that capacity for five years while continuing his service to Tobacco Valley District.

Judge Zelman has represented multi-national corporations in commercial litigation before state and federal courts. He knows how to handle probate administration and estate planning in ways that best serve his clients’ needs and goals. Clients appreciate his empathy and his ability to bring successful outcomes at times of high emotional distress. Prompt efficient attention to family issues in a time of loss is Judge Zelman’s paramount concern. The legal community, including judges and attorneys, frequently call on Steven to speak on a variety of probate issues, estate administration and commercial litigation.

attorneys.name: Nathan Craig Zezula
attorneys.practice_type: FINRA Arbitration Lawyers in Stamford, CT
attorneys.bio:
Nathan Zezula is an associate in Meister Seelig & Fein LLP's litigation department where his practice focuses on complex commercial litigation. Mr. Zezula's commercial litigation experience includes breach of contract claims, unfair trade practice claims, disputes arising from the sale of businesses, non-compete claims, real estate disputes and trade secret misappropriation claims, as well as fraud and breach of fiduciary duty claims. Mr. Zezula also has extensive experience in securing pre-judgment relief, including temporary injunctions and restraining orders. In addition, Mr. Zezula has represented clients in federal patent infringement disputes and bankruptcy adversary proceedings.

Mr. Zezula is admitted to practice in New York and Connecticut, as well as before the United States District Courts for the Southern and Eastern Districts of New York and the District of Connecticut.

Mr. Zezula received his B.A. from Tulane University and graduated magna cum laude from Pace Law School, where he was managing editor of the PACE LAW REVIEW. After law school Mr. Zezula clerked for the Honorable George A. Yanthis, Magistrate Judge, United States District Court, S.D.N.Y. Before joining Meister Seelig & Fein LLP, Mr. Zezula was an associate in the litigation department of Robinson & Cole LLP. Prior to embarking on his legal career, Mr. Zezula spent four years on active duty as an artillery officer in the United States Army in Germany and Kosovo, leaving with the rank of Captain.
